bib.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the ACL (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 1762-1777

question: Can an effective dense retriever be built with no relevance labels by having an instruction-following LM write a hypothetical document and encoding that with an unsupervised contrastive encoder?
hypothesis: Relevance modeling can be offloaded to a generative LM, and the encoder's dense bottleneck filters hallucinated details, giving performance near fine-tuned retrievers.
contributions: HyDE: pivot query through a generated hypothetical document embedded by an unsupervised contrastive encoder
Evaluation on web search, 7 BEIR tasks and 4 Mr.TyDi languages, beating Contriever and competitive with fine-tuned retrievers
Analysis of generator choice, base LMs, fine-tuned encoders

method.summary: For each query, prompt InstructGPT (text-davinci-003, temp 0.7) with a task-specific instruction to write a passage, encode N sampled passages (and optionally the query) with Contriever/mContriever, average the vectors, and retrieve by inner product over precomputed corpus embeddings using Pyserini. Nothing is trained.
method.task: zero-shot dense retrieval (web search, BEIR, multilingual)

datasets.name: TREC DL19
datasets.source: MS MARCO based; corpus 8.84M documents; MIT licence non-commercial

datasets.name: BEIR: Scifact, Arguana, TREC-COVID, FiQA, DBPedia, TREC-NEWS, Climate-Fever
datasets.size: corpora: Scifact 5K, Arguana 8.67K, TREC-COVID 171K, FiQA 57K, DBPedia 4.6M, TREC-NEWS 595K, Climate-Fever 5.4M docs

datasets.name: Mr.TyDi sw/ko/ja/bn
datasets.size: corpora: sw 136K, ko 1.5M, ja 7M, bn 300K docs

models.name: Contriever-ft / mContriever-ft, DPR, ANCE, mDPR, mBERT, XLM-R
models.architecture: fine-tuned on MS MARCO; numbers taken from BEIR, Mr.TyDi and Contriever papers

inference.samples: N samples per query, value of N not stated; no seeds or repeated runs stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot, one instruction per dataset (appendix A.1); 3-shot for base GPT-3 in Sec 5.2
inference.retrieval: inner product between averaged hypothetical-document vector (optionally plus query vector, 1/(N+1)) and corpus vectors; Pyserini; top-k depth for metrics per official metric

parameters.query_included_in_average: Eq 8 variant, whether used in reported runs not stated

eval.protocol: single reported number per cell; no seeds, error bars or significance tests stated

availability.weights: not applicable (no training); generator via API

results.claim: HyDE lifts Contriever nDCG@10 on TREC DL19 from 44.5 to 61.3, above BM25 (50.6).
results.setup: TREC DL19 (and DL20), MS MARCO corpus 8.84M passages; HyDE = text-davinci-003 (temp 0.7) + unsupervised Contriever (110M), no training; one fixed prompt; no seeds or run count stated
results.table: Table 1, row HyDE, column DL19 nDCG@10

results.claim: HyDE DL19 Recall@1k is 88.0 against 74.6 for Contriever and 75.0 for BM25, above the fine-tuned models.
results.setup: TREC DL19 (and DL20), MS MARCO corpus 8.84M passages; HyDE = text-davinci-003 (temp 0.7) + unsupervised Contriever (110M), no training; one fixed prompt; no seeds or run count stated
results.table: Table 1, row HyDE, column DL19 Recall@1k

results.claim: On DL20 HyDE nDCG@10 is 57.9, below Contriever-ft (63.2) but above Contriever (42.1) and BM25 (48.0).
results.setup: TREC DL19 (and DL20), MS MARCO corpus 8.84M passages; HyDE = text-davinci-003 (temp 0.7) + unsupervised Contriever (110M), no training; one fixed prompt; no seeds or run count stated
results.table: Table 1, row HyDE, column DL20 nDCG@10

results.claim: On DL19 DPR (62.2) and ANCE (64.5) beat HyDE (61.3) on nDCG@10 but have lower Recall@1k (76.9, 75.5).
results.setup: as Table 1; DPR/ANCE/Contriever-ft are fine-tuned on MS MARCO (in-domain)
results.table: Table 1, row ANCE, column DL19 nDCG@10
results.quote: The ANCE model shows better nDCG@10 numbers than HyDE but lower recall, suggesting it may be biased to a subset of queries and/or relevant documents.

results.claim: On seven BEIR low-resource tasks HyDE beats Contriever on nDCG@10 everywhere; e.g. TREC-COVID 59.3 vs 27.3, BM25 59.5.
results.setup: BEIR TREC-COVID; same HyDE setup; per-dataset instruction from appendix A.1
results.quote:
HyDE is only outper-
formed by BM25 on one dataset, TREC-COVID,
but by a tiny margin on nDCG@10

results.claim: HyDE on Arguana nDCG@10 is 46.6 vs 37.9 for Contriever and 44.6 for Contriever-ft.
Contriever-ft keeps an edge on FiQA (32.9 vs 27.3) and DBPedia (41.3 vs 36.8); authors attribute it to under-specified instructions.
results.quote:
We believe the performance differences can be at-
tributed to the under-specification of the instruc-
tions; more elaborate prompts may help.

results.claim: Multilingual (MRR@100, Mr.TyDi): HyDE beats mContriever in all four languages but trails mContriever-ft; Swahili 41.7 vs 38.3 vs 51.2.
results.setup: Mr.TyDi sw/ko/ja/bn; mContriever encoder; InstructGPT generator with 'in {language}' instruction

results.claim: Japanese shows the largest multilingual gain: HyDE 30.7 vs mContriever 19.5.
Generator size and instruction tuning matter: with Flan-T5-xxl (11B) DL19 nDCG@10 is 48.9, Cohere (52B) 53.8, InstructGPT 61.3.
results.setup: TREC DL19, Contriever encoder, swapped generator
results.table: Table 4, row w/ Flan-T5, column DL19 nDCG@10
results.quote:
Generally, we observe that all models bring
improvements to the unsupervised Contriever, with
larger models bringing bigger improvements.

limits: Relies on real-time LLM generation, so unsuitable for high-throughput or low-latency tasks (Limitations).
Generated content may carry LLM bias into search results.
Multilingual gap to mContriever-ft attributed to under-trained languages (hypothesis, not tested).
Only dense retrieval with Contriever-family encoders compared; BM25 only as baseline, no hybrid.
No run counts, seeds, variance or N stated; generator text-davinci-003 is a deprecated API model.
Prompts were written per dataset; no prompt sensitivity study.

terms.definition: Hypothetical Document Embeddings: encode an LM-generated hypothetical document in place of the query

lineage.work: Unsupervised dense information retrieval with contrastive learning (Contriever)
Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (InstructGPT)
Improving passage retrieval with zero-shot question generation (Sachan et al.)
Task-aware retrieval with instructions (Asai et al.)
Large dual encoders are generalizable retrievers (GTR)
